title: Jailer 2 Rises to Rs 443 Crore in India After Record Second Weekend
excerpt: Pinkvilla puts the Rajinikanth sequel at Rs. 443.25 crore India gross after 12 days and about Rs. 690 crore worldwide — already Kollywood's biggest film globally, with the India record in reach.
body:
• Jailer 2 has reached Rs. 443.25 crore gross in India after 12 days, up from Rs. 374 crore at the end of its first week, according to Pinkvilla trade estimates.
  • The second weekend added just over Rs. 69 crore gross, a drop of only about 55 per cent week on week — a strong hold for a film that opened this big.
  • Worldwide, the Rajinikanth starrer stands at about Rs. 690 crore gross, making it the biggest Kollywood film of all time globally, ahead of 2.0 at Rs. 663 crore.
  • On net figures tracked by Koimoi, the film's Rs. 64.35 crore second weekend is Kollywood's biggest ever, beating 2.0's Rs. 53.1 crore.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has risen to Rs. 443.25 crore gross in India after a strong second weekend, according to Pinkvilla's box office tracking. The film collected about Rs. 27.25 crore on its second Sunday, closing the weekend at just over Rs. 69 crore. That is a fall of around 55 per cent from its opening weekend — a hold Pinkvilla describes as superb for a South Indian film, and stronger still given the scale of the opening.

The update moves the story well past where it stood three days ago. The Videshi previously reported the film crossing Rs. 600 crore worldwide with India gross at Rs. 374 crore. The worldwide total now stands at about Rs. 690 crore gross, which Pinkvilla says makes Jailer 2 the biggest Kollywood film of all time worldwide, surpassing 2.0 at Rs. 663 crore.

Where the money came from

Tamil Nadu remains the film's engine, with Rs. 166.25 crore gross and, according to Pinkvilla, a clear path to more than Rs. 200 crore over the full run. The performance outside the home state is the bigger story. The Telugu states (APTS) have contributed Rs. 83 crore, Karnataka Rs. 78.25 crore and Kerala Rs. 71 crore, with Pinkvilla reporting that Karnataka and Kerala have already recorded the biggest grosses ever for a Kollywood film. The Telugu states are less than Rs. 10 crore short of the 2.0 record. The rest of India accounts for Rs. 44.75 crore.

The Hindi dubbed version has also held up despite a limited release. Pinkvilla puts it at Rs. 33 crore nett so far, heading for a close above Rs. 40 crore nett — a strong return, the tracker notes, for a dubbed film released with little spending and without the high-collecting national chains.

Gross and net tell the same story

Trackers report the run on different bases, and the two sets of figures are consistent once that is allowed for. Koimoi, reporting India net, put the film at Rs. 398.7 crore after 11 days and credited its Rs. 64.35 crore second weekend as the biggest second weekend ever for a Kollywood film in India, ahead of 2.0 (Rs. 53.1 crore), the first Jailer (Rs. 45.75 crore) and Ponniyin Selvan 2 (Rs. 40.15 crore). On the gross measure Pinkvilla uses, the film already ranks as the second-highest-grossing Kollywood film in India, behind only 2.0, and is expected to take the top spot shortly.

The film and what comes next

Jailer 2 is the Tamil-language sequel directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, with Rajinikanth returning in the lead alongside an ensemble that includes Ramya Krishnan and Mohanlal. It opened on a Thursday to Rs. 67.50 crore gross in India, the biggest day of its run so far, and crossed Rs. 400 crore gross in India within 10 days.

For diaspora audiences, the run matters beyond the records. Tamil films now routinely open day-and-date across North America, the Gulf, Malaysia and Singapore, and a Kollywood title passing Rs. 690 crore worldwide underlines how much of that total is earned outside India. The next test is the third weekend: whether the film's weekday holds keep it on course for the India gross record Pinkvilla expects, and how far past Rs. 700 crore worldwide it can travel before new releases take its screens. Pinkvilla notes its figures are trade estimates compiled from commercial parameters, not certified collections.
